messages:
julia: Heads-up — FinOps dash flagged a big EU on-demand GPU spend spike yesterday ~03:00 UTC. Reserved pool utilization for p4d dropped to ~58% while on-demand instances jumped. Screenshot attached in the dash. cc @lisa-finops @ben-ops :eyes:

lisa-finops: I pulled the per-model view — most of the cost is from the /api/generate route for model redwood-large-v2 in eu-west1-dev. Cost/token went up ~2.1x during the window. Query I ran: 
```
SELECT route, model, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM finops.route_costs
WHERE region='eu-west1' AND ts >= '2026-03-15' AND ts < '2026-03-16'
GROUP BY route, model
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
Link to raw rows: <https://console.redwood/finops/rows?run=4729> :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ben-ops: Any config changes around that time? autoscaler, canaries, or rollout? Could be a scaling loop causing short-lived instances.

danny: We had a canary scale tweak rolled out at 02:45 UTC to allow more aggressive burst for canary traffic (policy `canary-burst-v2`). Might be related. I can check instance lifetime histograms.

zara: From the infra logs I see a spike in short-lived VM launches (avg lifetime 10-12m) in eu-west1 at 02:50-03:20. Also a surge in 429 retries from the gateway going to the nodes. That would inflate GPU billed time.

op-corp-billing-bot: Alert: egress & compute line items exceeded daily threshold (rule: region_costs/eu-west1). See billing export blob `billing-2026-03-15-eu.csv`.

amar: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) scaling policy created extra on-demand capacity instead of using reserved pool; 2) failing requests caused retries and long tail GPU utilization. Also check whether preemptible instances were used (billing label `preemptible=false`).

lisa-finops: Action items I propose: add a per-route burn-rate chart to the daily dash (tokens/cost over time), show reserved vs on-demand ratio by pool, and add a column for 'avg instance lifetime'. I'll create a dashboard PR unless someone objects.

julia: No objections. Also can we enrich the billing export join to include `scaling_policy` and `instance_lifetime` so we can attribute cost to policy changes? Example join snippet I used: 
```
SELECT b.*, s.policy_name, i.lifetime
FROM billing_export b
LEFT JOIN scaler_events s ON b.instance_id = s.instance_id
LEFT JOIN instance_hist i ON b.instance_id = i.instance_id
```

ben-ops: I'll rollback the burst change for `canary-burst-v2` to yesterday's config and monitor. Assigning to @danny and @zara to validate. ETA ~4h. :hammer_and_wrench:

danny: Got it — will also grep autoscaler logs for duplicate create/destroy loops and attach short-run instance ids to the ticket.

zara: I'll surface the gateway 429s timeline to the app team; retries probably multiplied GPU time. Also checking network peering logs for transient errors around 02:48.

lisa-finops: For forecasting: if this repeats, our reserved recommendation for eu-west1 p4d should move from monthly on-demand buffer to a 6-month partial commit. I'll run a sensitivity calc once we confirm root cause.

julia: I've opened INF-4821 with the initial notes + logs link: <https://issues.redwood/INF-4821>. Please drop any IDs in the ticket.

ben-ops: Next steps: (1) rollback canary burst (done by EOD), (2) infra to attach instance lifetimes & scaler traces to INF-4821, (3) finops to update dash + run reserved-sensitivity calc. We'll reconvene in #finops in ~6h. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

lisa-finops: I'll also push a temporary alert: reserved_utilization < 70% AND on_demand_spend > baseline*1.5 -> page on-call. If we get repeats we escalate to capacity planning sync.

julia: Thanks all — keep updates in the ticket and ping here if anything urgent. :pray:
